The data are DESI DR1 blue-arm spectra: over 420,000 Lyman-alpha forests (twice the SDSS DR16 sample) and more than 700,000 quasars at z > 1.77 as tracers. The method measures four 3D two-point functions (the region-A forest auto-correlation, the region-A x region-B forest correlation, and the cross-correlations of each forest region with quasar positions; the noisy B-region auto-correlation is dropped), fits them jointly with the Vega code including, for the first time, the cross-covariance between auto- and cross-correlations, and marginalises over 15 nuisance parameters for metals, high-column-density absorbers, redshift errors and pipeline noise. The result at z_eff = 2.33 is D_H/r_d = 8.52 +/- 0.17 and D_M/r_d = 39.71 +/- 0.95 (2.0% and 2.4% precision), i.e. H(z_eff) = 239.2 +/- 4.8 km/s/Mpc for r_d = 147.09 Mpc, with the cross-correlation now dominating. cards.title: Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters
cards.abstract: arXiv:1807.06209. This is the final Planck Collaboration paper on cosmological parameters. It asks how well six-parameter flat ΛCDM describes the full-mission CMB temperature, polarization and lensing data, and whether any common extension is preferred. The data are the 2018 HFI/LFI maps, with a new low-multipole polarization likelihood that pins the reionization optical depth (τ = 0.054 ± 0.007) and two high-multipole TT,TE,EE likelihoods (Plik, CamSpec) built from the same Planck maps but with different corrections for polarization systematics; their differences bound residual systematics at the ≲0.5σ level. Parameters are sampled with CosmoMC using CAMB spectra, and the CMB is combined with galaxy BAO (6dFGS, SDSS-MGS, BOSS DR12), Pantheon supernovae, RSD, DES lensing and BBN. The headline result is that base ΛCDM fits everything well: H0 = 67.4 ± 0.5 km/s/Mpc, Ωm = 0.315 ± 0.007, σ8 = 0.811 ± 0.006, ns = 0.965 ± 0.004, and with BAO the Universe is flat to ΩK = 0.0007 ± 0.0019, w0 = −1.03 ± 0.03 with SNe, Σmν < 0.12 eV and Neff = 2.99 ± 0.17. No extension is favoured. What remains open are the tensions: a 4.4σ gap with distance-ladder H0, a Lyα BAO offset at z ≈ 2.4 that was about 2.3σ for the superseded SDSS DR12 data (the conclusions quote "about 2.5σ" without naming a release) but 1.7σ for the combined DR14 DM/rdrag value in Sec. 5.1, a 2.5σ lower S8 from DES clustering, and an internal preference for more lensing smoothing (AL > 1) that the lensing reconstruction does not support (its curvature counterpart BAO pulls back to flat). The paper leaves unresolved whether these are systematics, fluctuations or new physics.
